description:
`http-to-smtp` is the inverse of `smtp-to-http`: POST a message to the UnitySVC API Gateway and it is delivered as a real email through an SMTP server you control.

The gateway terminates the request on the platform-native `notify://smtp` upstream — there is no seller endpoint to call. It accepts either the compact `{title, body, type, format}` `msg` envelope or the faithful `email` payload the SMTP-to-HTTP converter emits (sender, recipients, subject, text and html bodies, threading headers, base64 attachments), reconstructs a MIME message from it, and submits that message to your SMTP server. Because delivery is queued, a 2xx means accepted for delivery, not delivered — the same contract the SMTP gateway's own `250` carries.

Use the free `byok` channel to send through one SMTP server stored in customer secrets (`HTTP_TO_SMTP_HOST`, `HTTP_TO_SMTP_PORT`, `HTTP_TO_SMTP_TLS`, `HTTP_TO_SMTP_USERNAME`, `HTTP_TO_SMTP_PASSWORD`, `HTTP_TO_SMTP_FROM`, `HTTP_TO_SMTP_TO`). Use the metered `plus` channel to run many SMTP destinations under one account: each enrollment binds its own host, port, TLS mode, sender and recipient, names the secrets holding its credentials, is reached at a unique `/e/<code>` URL, and is billed at $1 per 1,000 messages. To send through the UnitySVC SMTP gateway rather than your own server, use the http-to-smtp-gateway service instead. See “How to use this service” for setup and examples.
name: http-to-smtp

payout_price.description: No platform commission — customer uses own SMTP server
